resources.string: Connect an AI service, then choose the model MiniRP will use for chats and preset setup.
A provider is the service that runs your model. Choose its template to fill in the connection details. If the service needs an API key, get it from the provider’s website.
Pick a model from %1$s to use for your first conversations.
Check the API address and key, then try again. If your provider doesn’t list models, enter the exact model ID from its website.

Thinking effort is how much time your AI spends working things out before it replies. For a complicated story or a plugin, start with the highest level. For a quick chat, try a lower one. Higher levels can take longer and use more of your plan’s quota. You can change this anytime in Settings → Models.
Copy this prompt into %1$s, then follow the steps it gives you.
I’m new to MiniRP for Android. Please reply in %1$s. My device region is %2$s. First read the official MiniRP guide at %3$s. Let me know if you can’t open it.

Help me connect a model to MiniRP. I’m new to this. MiniRP is a native agentic RP harness built on the coding-agent pattern. Its agents run multi-step tasks, use tools to work with code and files, and delegate to subagents. Treat it as a third-party agent harness when checking plan compatibility. It can directly use Coding Plans, Agent Plans, and other AI subscriptions that provide a compatible model API. Check the plan’s rules for the client and the work I want to do. MiniRP supports OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Google Gemini, and Ollama. Match the exact protocol, subscription Base URL, and model ID. Show me where to sign up, which provider template to choose or what name to enter, what to put in each field, and how to select the model after saving.

Help me decide whether to set up web search (real_search) and page fetch (real_fetch) in MiniRP for Android. Under Settings → Search and fetch APIs, I can choose each provider separately and enter its key. Search supports DeepSeek, Tavily, Exa, and Brave Search. Fetch supports DeepSeek, Tavily, and Exa. When DeepSeek is selected, MiniRP can reuse the key from a saved DeepSeek model provider. Without a search key, MiniRP tries Mwmbl and then the built-in browser. The browser can also fetch pages. Search the web for current official documentation and reviews from developers. Recommend options for my account and region, then show how to test search and fetch using a public page.

Use live web searches as of today. If browsing is unavailable, ask me to enable it before recommending anything. Ask where I’ll use MiniRP, what I’ll use it for, and my budget. For mainland China, check registration and access separately. Look at current official terms, integration docs, and pricing, plus recent firsthand reports from developers who connected the service. Include Coding Plans, Agent Plans, and other subscriptions with direct API access and relevant free or usage-based options. For each subscription, say whether the official terms explicitly permit this use, are silent but developers report success, explicitly prohibit it, or could not be verified. Developer reports establish technical compatibility, while permission comes from the provider. Check the subscription endpoint against the regular usage-based endpoint, and explain monthly price, included API usage, limits, and what happens when the quota runs out. Link the official sources and developer reports with dates. Use plain language and recommend one or two options with the clearest permission and easiest setup. Guide me through one action at a time.
Ask me to enter secrets only in the provider’s website or in MiniRP. Never ask me to send you API keys, verification codes, or payment details.
